title: To know one another
hook: We made you nations and tribes to know one another, and the most honored is the most mindful (49:13)
carry: made different to know each other

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was ghibah, backbiting, even when what's said is true. Your line: not behind their back.

Arabic, Urdu, Malay, Turkish, Swahili, Hausa, Bosnian, French, English with a Texas accent. During the pilgrimage, all of it rises from one courtyard in Mecca, from faces of every shade in the same white cloth. The Qur'an has a verse about why humanity comes in so many kinds. It's in Surah Al-Hujurat, and for once in this surah it isn't addressed to believers. It's addressed to everyone.

Again and again, this surah has called: O ye who believe. Verse thirteen opens wider. Pickthall's translation: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct." Three moves. One origin: male and female, which commentators read as Adam and Hawwa, one family. Deliberate difference: nations and tribes, made on purpose. And the purpose, in one Arabic word: li-ta'arafu, so that you may know one another. The verb's form means mutual knowing, each side learning the other. Its root is shared with ma'ruf, the known good, and 'urf, custom. Difference here isn't a problem to solve. It's an introduction. Then the ranking is taken away from everything you can see. The noblest is the most mindful; the Arabic is atqakum, from taqwa, awareness of God. Not the richest, not the oldest family, not the right tribe. And taqwa can't be seen from outside; the verse leaves that judgment to the sight of Allah. A sermon attributed to the Prophet ﷺ during his farewell pilgrimage, recorded in the Musnad of Ahmad, put it plainly: no Arab has merit over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, nor red over black, nor black over red, except by taqwa. This week was the surah's lesson in talking well: a pledge, a lower voice, checked news, peace made, mocking dropped, backbiting refused. It ends with why the people across the table are different in the first place.
screen: `O MANKIND: THE VERSE OPENS WIDER.` · `ONE ORIGIN, DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE.` · `LI-TA'ARAFU: KNOWING EACH OTHER.` · `THE NOBLEST: THE MOST MINDFUL.`

segments.voice: Picture someone you see often whose background differs from yours: a neighbor, a coworker, the person who runs the shop on the corner. Think about what you actually know of where they come from, maybe not much, and choose one kind question you'd like to ask them: a food, a holiday, a word in their language. If you pray, you can thank Allah for the variety of people.
Taqwa: the awareness of God, the only thing by which 49:13 says anyone is more noble than another. Today's word.
Your line: made different to know each other. Day five hundred eighty-eight, and a week complete.

howItsDone: Muslims cite 49:13 against racism and tribalism, and the farewell sermon's words on Arab and non-Arab, red and black, are read in Friday sermons and at the pilgrimage.

chat.says: What does the Qur'an say about why people come in so many nations and races?
options: So we'd know one another; the noblest is the most mindful of God.
So each nation keeps to itself and protects its own customs.
So the people who first received the Qur'an could lead the rest.
